claims: The focus guard misses lock-disabled gate runs — `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:601`: under `--no-lock` or `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK=0`, no mapped command carries `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD`, and the guard at line 601 does not fire
`acquire_gate_run_lock` returns at `scripts/agent-quality-gate.sh:1617` before the only `export AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` at `scripts/agent-quality-gate.sh:1143`

developer with `export GATE_TEST_FOCUS=gate-contract` runs `pnpm agent:quality-gate --run --no-lock` → the mapped self-test runs one 2s family, prints `agent quality gate focused tests passed: gate-contract`, exits 0, and the gate records the self-test as passed

The new doc text is wrong on the same point: `docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1144` claims `AGENT_QUALITY_GATE_LOCK_HELD` is set by "any command a real gate run spawns", which line 594–596 of that same file contradicts

The partition checker never asserts the dispatch call exists — `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:554-563`: Line 515 permits `dispatch_gate_test_families` after the end marker without ever requiring it, and the `END` block checks `seen_end` but has no `seen_dispatch`

I deleted the final `dispatch_gate_test_families` line and ran the file. The partition check passed, zero tests ran, nothing was printed, and it exited 0 — and since the self-test is stamp-exempt but not output-checked, the gate would report it as passed

`arm_suite_abort_trap` is required but unenforced — `scripts/agent-quality-gate.test.sh:520`: a 12th family added without it runs with no ERR trap, since bash does not inherit it into functions; consequence is lost diagnostics on abort
`docs/notes/agent-quality-gate-mechanics.md:1116` says "the whole ~9-minute suite", but the solo runtimes in the table immediately below sum to 696s ≈ 11.6 min
